newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Visitors to HK up 15.6 percent in 1H 96 versus 95.
newsitem.headline: Visitors to HK up 15.6 percent in 1H 96 versus 95.

text.p: Hong Kong Tourist Association said on Friday visitor arrivals to the colony grew 15.6 percent between January and June 1996 versus the same period in 1995.

Arrivals reached 5.4 million, with increases seen from all major markets, except Taiwan, which fell 14.3 percent to just over 720,000 due to competition from Macau, which opened its airport at the end of 1995.
Arrivals from North Asia rose 38.3 percent to 1.2 million, while those from China hit 1.1 million, up 8.4 percent.
Some 658,000 visitors were from Europe, Africa and the Middle East, up 11.5 percent, while those from the Americas grew 0.4 percent to 485,000.
Visitors from Australia, New Zealand and the South Pacific hit almost 196,500, up 19.9 percent.
Arrivals in June grew 16.0 percent versus June 1995.
The association forecasts an increase of around 10 percent to 11.4 million in arrivals for the whole of 1996 versus 1995.
